clarity_findings.claim: The guide map's brief item 2 for this page ("Moons orbit planets and gas giants. Asteroids sit in belts. Gas giants and belts have no tiles.") is never stated in prose.
clarity_findings.problem: A reader has to reverse-engineer the orbit relationships and which bodies have zero tiles from the generated body-types table's "Tiles" and "Orbiting bodies" columns (e.g. seeing "Gas giant / Tiles 0 / Orbiting bodies 1-3 Moon") rather than being told directly. This is a reading stumble, not a rule violation and not accuracy-critic territory since the page owns this fact and simply leaves it implicit.
clarity_findings.fix: Add one short sentence after the body-types table, e.g. "Moons orbit planets and gas giants. Asteroids sit in belts. Gas giants and belts have no tiles."

clarity_findings.claim: The infrastructure-tile section states the rule but never points forward to where a curious reader learns more about tile/building mechanics.
clarity_findings.problem: The brief for this section calls for "One sentence plus a link to the building page" alongside the rule that other tiles need the infrastructure building and that upgrades cap at its level (owned by Buildings). The page states the tile-1 rule but gives the reader no [[link]] onward, so a reader who wonders "what about the other tiles?" has nowhere to go from this page.
clarity_findings.fix: Add a short pointer sentence such as "See [[production]]." or the relevant Buildings leaf once it exists, per rule 4 (point instead of half-explaining).

votes.reason: Well-organized (screenshot, clear tables, a footnote resolving the scaling notation), but a couple of phrasing/mapping gaps make a careful player pause and reread.
stumbles: The screenshot caption says "its three potentials (1)" but never names which icon (gear/flask/triangle) is Industrial vs Scientific vs Appeal, so a player can't map the picture's "4 / 2 / 2" numbers to the potential names below.

"+3 → +15 Production per Industrial Potential" reads ambiguously on first pass — it's not obvious the arrow tracks the building's level while "per Industrial Potential" is a separate multiplier on the body's stat, until you reach the footnote below the table.

"Outside a daily, your first system always has the same bodies, so it can fall outside these ranges." assumes the reader already knows what "a daily" is; the sentence's logic (why being outside a daily makes ranges not apply) isn't spelled out on this page.

votes.reason: The annotated screenshot and body/star tables make tiles, the infrastructure tile, and the three potentials clear in one pass; only the dense per-building scaling numbers and the closing daily-mode caveat need a second look.
stumbles: "+3 → +15 Production per Industrial Potential; +6 → +30 Credit per Industrial Potential" packs level-scaling and per-potential scaling into one line, so it takes a beat to parse which number moves with building level vs. planet potential

"Outside a daily, your first system always has the same bodies, so it can fall outside these ranges." assumes the reader already knows what "a daily" is; a first-time reader has to pause to work out the exception
Body-type table gives Moon appeal potential as 1–4 while Asteroid gives 1–5 (and vice-versa for scientific) with no callout, so the asymmetry is easy to skim past without registering
